turn.subject: discharge-chain
turn.user_message: Discharge delays. Our patients are medically fit by mid-morning but most don’t leave till late afternoon.

text: Before I suggest anything, I want to see how discharge really runs in your hospital. Most delays that look like discharge problems start further up the chain.
First stop, the doctors: who writes the discharge summary, who reviews it, who signs it — and when do rounds finish on your busiest wards?
chat.pointer: The whole route is laid out for you — tap any stop to see what I’ll ask there.
chat.note: Most delays start long before the billing desk.

points.label: The doctors — who writes, reviews and signs
Nurses — when they count used supplies
Pharmacy — returns counted by hand or system

prompts: A junior doctor writes it, the consultant signs

blocks.title: The road to going home
blocks.deck: Eleven stops, each run by a different team. We walk them one at a time.

stations.name: The doctors
stations.text: The summary is drafted, reviewed and signed by different people. The round decides when any of it can start.
stations.question: Who writes the summary, who reviews it, who signs it — and when do rounds finish?

stations.name: Supply count
stations.text: The bill can’t be finished until nurses count the used supplies, and they count only when free.
stations.question: How long after the doctor signs do nurses start counting supplies?

stations.name: Pharmacy returns
stations.text: What was issued, used and can be credited back. Counted by hand, it forces a second pass on the bill.
stations.question: Is the returnable balance worked out by the system or by a nurse?

stations.name: Billing
stations.text: A charge that lands after the bill is closed reopens it.
stations.question: How many bills were reopened after closing last month?

stations.name: Insurance desk
stations.text: The insurer’s approval window sits inside the family’s wait.
stations.question: Does your discharge time include the whole wait for insurance?

stations.name: Bed desk
stations.text: Discharge times can only be checked against when beds are given out.
stations.question: Can the bed desk tell me when those beds were given out?

stations.name: Housekeeping
stations.text: A bed turns from when housekeeping is told, not when the patient left.
stations.question: How long from the patient leaving to housekeeping being told?

stations.name: Transport
stations.text: Porters are shared with admissions and diagnostics at the same peak.
stations.question: How many porters are on duty at the discharge peak?

stations.name: Operating theatre
stations.text: A bed freed late can’t be used for a same-day operation.
stations.question: What’s the latest hour a freed bed can still be used for an operation that day?

stations.name: Briefing chain
stations.text: Dietitian, pharmacist and nurse must each see the patient, in no set order.
stations.question: Who has to see the patient before they leave?

stations.name: Cash counter
stations.text: Every discharge meets one counter in a two-hour window.
stations.question: Who can release a patient with a balance due?
